x: It is a coordination forum for debtor nations launched by developing countries, not a debt restructuring mechanism.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the World Bank's Water Forward programme?
o: It seeks water security for 1 billion people by 2030
It is delivered through country-led Water Compacts
The World Bank Group alone is to reach 600 million of the 1 billion
It was launched by WBG President Ajay Banga
x: The World Bank Group is to reach 400 million people and partners 600 million; the other statements are correct.

s: Where was the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14) in March 2026 held?
x: MC14 was held at Yaoundé, Cameroon, on 26–29 March 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO's MC14:
1. It ended without agreement on WTO reform.
2. It renewed the e-commerce customs duty moratorium.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: MC14 ended without agreement on its main issues, and the e-commerce moratorium was not renewed and lapsed.

s: Under WTO rules, under the criteria of which box does public stockholding for food security fall?
x: Public stockholding for food security falls in the Green Box criteria; trade-distorting price support is Amber.

s: What is the Amber Box de minimis limit for developing countries?
x: The Amber Box de minimis is 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Dunkel Draft (20 December 1991) was the Uruguay Round Draft Final Act, not a Doha Round text.

s: How many members does the World Bank Group have?
x: The World Bank Group has 189 members; the World Bank was set up in 1944.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five arms of the World Bank Group?
x: The five arms are IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID; the AIIB is not part of the World Bank Group.

s: In its April 2026 World Economic Outlook, what growth did the IMF project for India for FY27?
x: The April 2026 WEO projected India's growth at 6.5% for FY27 and cut global growth for 2026 to 3.1%.

s: Who is the President of the World Bank Group who launched 'Water Forward' in April 2026?
x: WBG President Ajay Banga launched Water Forward on 15 April 2026.

s: Who, as IMF Managing Director, urged completion of the 16th General Review of Quotas in April 2026?
x: IMF MD Kristalina Georgieva urged completion of the 16th General Review of Quotas at the 2026 Spring Meetings.

s: Which currency has the second-largest weight in the IMF's SDR basket?
x: The SDR weights are: US dollar 43.38%, euro 29.31%, renminbi 12.28%, yen 7.59%, pound 7.44%.

s: What is India's voting share in the IMF?
x: India's quota is about 2.75% (SDR 13,114.4 million) and its voting share about 2.63%; it is the 8th-largest quota holder.

s: The World Bank's USD 299.66 million Clean Air Management Program (March 2026) is for which state?
x: The UP Clean Air Management Program, signed on 16 March 2026, is part of the Indo-Gangetic Plains air quality programme.

s: India's first World Bank Step-Up Loan (April 2026) was approved for:
x: The USD 225 million Rajasthan Highway Modernisation Project is India's first Step-Up Loan.

s: Which of the following is the Borrowers' Platform launched at the IMF–World Bank Spring Meetings 2026 NOT?
o: A forum to strengthen debt management
A coordination forum for debtor nations
x: The Borrowers' Platform is a coordination forum for debtor nations, not a debt restructuring mechanism.

s: How many WTO members decided at MC14 to implement the already-negotiated plurilateral e-commerce agreement?
x: At MC14 (Yaoundé, March 2026), 66 WTO members decided to implement the plurilateral e-commerce agreement.

s: What was India's rank in the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023?
x: India ranked 38th of 139 countries in LPI 2023, up six places from 44th in 2018.

s: What is the capital of Trinidad and Tobago, visited by S. Jaishankar?
x: The capital of Trinidad and Tobago is Port of Spain, not San Fernando.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Turkey's proposed social media curbs?
o: The Bill restricts social media for children below 15
The capital of Turkey is Istanbul
Platforms such as YouTube and TikTok must verify age
The Bill provides for parental controls
x: The capital of Turkey is Ankara, not Istanbul; the Bill restricts social media for children below 15.

s: Where is the European Investment Bank, which is financing coaches for Bangladesh, headquartered?
x: The EIB is headquartered in Luxembourg, not Brussels.

s: In which year was the India–EU Trade and Technology Council, under which the EV Battery Recycling initiative runs, launched?
x: The India–EU TTC was launched in 2022; the €15.2 million battery recycling initiative operates under it.

s: Whose signature will appear on US currency notes from June 2026, the first time for a sitting President?
x: Donald Trump's signature will appear first on the $100 note in June 2026, marking the 250th Independence Day.

s: India supplied 1,000 MT of rice as aid to which country?
x: India sent 1,000 MT rice to Burkina Faso; Seychelles received 250 MT food grains.

s: Which ministry launched the FAME scheme for electric vehicles in 2015?
x: FAME was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

s: What is the capital of Burkina Faso, to which India sent 1,000 MT of rice?
x: Ouagadougou is the capital of Burkina Faso; its Head of State is Ibrahim Traore.

s: Which Prime Minister declared a national emergency in Trinidad and Tobago in February 2024 over an oil spill off Tobago?
x: PM Keith Rowley declared a national emergency after the capsized barge Gulfstream leaked oil off Tobago in February 2024.

s: Off the coast of which island did the capsized barge Gulfstream cause an oil spill in February 2024?
x: The Gulfstream barge capsized on a reef off Tobago's south-west coast, leading Trinidad and Tobago to declare a national emergency.

s: Under the India–EU FTA, the EU offered commitments in how many services subsectors?
x: The EU offered commitments in 144 services subsectors and India in 102.

s: From which year is the EU's Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) to apply?
x: The CSDDD applies from 2027; the EUDR concerns deforestation after 2020.

s: Which trade agreement was concluded after negotiations between India and the European Union in January 2026?
x: India and the European Union concluded negotiations on a comprehensive Free Trade Agreement. The India–Mauritius CECPA, India–UAE CEPA and India–UK CETA were other FTAs listed for 2021–2025, not the agreement concluded with the EU in 2026.

s: After legal scrubbing, the India–EU FTA must be ratified by the European Parliament and how many EU member states?
x: Ratification is by the 27 EU member states and the European Parliament.

s: Under the India–EU FTA, which group of Indian exports is expected to gain most, with about USD 33 billion of exports becoming duty-free?
o: Textiles, apparel, leather, footwear and gems and jewellery
x: Labour-intensive sectors such as textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, marine products, gems and jewellery are expected to benefit from removal of 4–26% tariffs. Dairy, cereals, poultry and soymeal are protected sectors.

s: Under the India–EU FTA, rules-of-origin flexibility was provided for shrimps and which downstream product?
x: The flexibility covers shrimps and downstream aluminium, not cement.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Eurozone and Bulgaria?
o: The Eurozone had 20 members before Bulgaria joined
Bulgaria is scheduled to join the Eurozone in 2027
Bulgaria replaced the lev with the euro
Bulgaria became the 21st EU country to adopt the euro
x: Bulgaria joined the Eurozone in 2026, not 2027, becoming the 21st member after the earlier 20.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India–Euratom Agreement?
o: It covers peaceful, civilian nuclear cooperation
Euratom was set up in 1957 by the Treaty of Rome
x: India–Euratom cooperation is civilian only; Euratom is headquartered in Brussels, not Geneva.

s: Which FTA partner of India, in number, is the European Union?
x: The EU is India's 22nd FTA partner; India has 15 FTAs covering 27 countries.

s: Under the India–EU FTA, what share of India's exports become duty-free at once?
x: 90.7% of India's exports become duty-free at once; 92.1% and 97% are the tariff lines liberalised by India and the EU.

s: From which date did Bulgaria and Romania become full members of the Schengen area?
x: Bulgaria and Romania became full Schengen members from 1 January 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT among the sectors India protected under the India–EU FTA?
x: India protected dairy, cereals, poultry and soymeal; textiles are among the labour-intensive gainers.

s: How many non-EU countries are part of the Schengen area?
x: The Schengen area includes four non-EU states; Bulgaria and Romania became full Schengen members on 1 January 2025.

s:
Arrange the following stages of European integration in chronological order:
1. Treaties of Rome
2. European Coal and Steel Community
3. Maastricht Treaty
4. Brexit
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: ECSC 1951, Treaties of Rome 1957, Maastricht 1992 and Brexit 2020.

s: What is India's status in CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research?
x: India is an associate member of CERN.

s: What share of tariff lines did the EU liberalise under the India-EU FTA concluded in January 2026?
x: The EU liberalised 97% of tariff lines and India 92.1%; 90.7% of India's exports become duty-free at once.

s: Which trade deal concluded in January 2026 was called the 'Mother of All Deals'?
x: The India-EU FTA, concluded in January 2026, was called the 'Mother of All Deals'.

s: Which is India's largest goods trading partner, with goods trade of about USD 135 billion in FY24?
x: The EU is India's largest goods partner, about USD 135 billion (FY24); services about USD 53 billion.

s: What was the value of India-EU goods trade in FY24?
x: India-EU goods trade was about USD 135 billion in FY24; total bilateral trade was about USD 190 billion in 2024-25.

s: Which of the following sectors is NOT covered by the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) as given for Indian exports?
x: CBAM covers steel, aluminium, cement and chemicals; Indian steel may face a 20-35% cost rise from 2026.

s: Which two agreements run alongside the India-EU FTA?
o: Investment Protection Agreement and GI Agreement
Social Security Agreement and Migration Pact
Digital Trade Agreement and Space Agreement
x: The India-EU FTA runs alongside an Investment Protection Agreement and a Geographical Indications (GI) Agreement.

s: Operation Atalanta, with which India cooperates, is run by which of the following?
x: Operation Atalanta is run by the EU naval force (EUNAVFOR).

s: What does the EU Stability and Growth Pact limit?
o: Tariffs on imports from third countries
x: The EU Stability and Growth Pact limits budget deficits.

s: Which trade agreement carries a USD 100 billion FDI commitment?
x: The India–EFTA TEPA carries the USD 100 billion FDI commitment.

s: In which city did India and the GCC sign the Terms of Reference to restart FTA negotiations in February 2026?
x: India and the GCC signed the Terms of Reference for the FTA in New Delhi, marking the restart of negotiations; Raja Al Marzouqi was the GCC chief negotiator.

s: The India–Oman CEPA is India's second CEPA with a GCC country. With which country was its first, in 2022?
x: The first was the India–UAE CEPA of 2022.

s: Which of the following was NOT excluded by India from its commitments under the India–Oman CEPA?
o: Gold and silver bullion and jewellery
x: India's exclusions include dairy, tea, bullion and jewellery, footwear and sports goods; petroleum and crude are not excluded.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India–Oman CEPA?
o: The Intra-Corporate Transferees quota was raised from 20% to 40%
Oman gives India duty-free access across 98.08% of tariff lines
India liberalised 77.79% of its tariff lines for Oman
Contractual Service Suppliers get a stay of two years, extendable by two years
x: The Intra-Corporate Transferees quota rose from 20% to 50%, not 40%.

s: Exercise Naseem Al Bahr is a bilateral naval exercise between India and which country?
x: Naseem Al Bahr is the India–Oman bilateral naval exercise held since 1993; Oman was the first GCC country to hold a bilateral naval exercise with India.

s: Which of the following pairs related to Oman is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Rub al-Khali – Mountain range in northern Oman
x: Rub al-Khali is the Empty Quarter; the mountain range in northern Oman is the Hajar Mountains. Muscat is the capital and Yemen borders Oman.

s: Which of the following pairs of India's trade agreements is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: CECPA is with Mauritius (2021); the UAE agreement is a CEPA (2022).

s: Where is the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), with which India restarted FTA talks in 2026, headquartered?
x: The GCC, established in 1981, is headquartered in Riyadh.

s: With which country was India's first trade agreement with an African nation, the 2021 CECPA, signed?
x: The India–Mauritius CECPA (2021) was India's first trade pact with an African nation.

s: Under the India–Oman CEPA, to what level does the quota for Intra-Corporate Transferees rise from 20%?
x: The Mode 4 quota for Intra-Corporate Transferees rises from 20% to 50%.

s: Which country is described as the oldest independent state in the Arab world?
x: Oman, capital Muscat, is the oldest independent state in the Arab world.

s: Which Indian traditional-medicine sector got dedicated annexures in India's trade agreements with Oman and New Zealand?
x: AYUSH got dedicated annexures in the trade agreements with Oman and New Zealand, finalised in December 2025.

s: The India-Oman CEPA is Oman's first bilateral trade agreement since which year?
x: The India-Oman CEPA is Oman's first bilateral trade agreement since 2006.

s: From 1 January 2026, India assumed which position in International IDEA?
x: India assumed the chairmanship of International IDEA from 1 January 2026 at a Council meeting in Stockholm, represented by CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

s: In which category was India re-elected to the IMO Council for 2026–27, with 154 of 169 votes?
x: India was re-elected to the IMO Council in Category B with the highest votes, 154 of 169.

s: Who became the first Indian Chair of the UN Advisory Board on Disarmament Matters for 2026–27?
x: D.B. Venkatesh Varma became the first Indian Chair of the ABDM for 2026–27.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Maritime Organization located?
x: The International Maritime Organization was established in 1948 and is headquartered in London. Stockholm, Geneva and New York are not the IMO headquarters.

s: With what does the High-level Political Forum run by the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) deal?
x: ECOSOC runs the High-level Political Forum on the Sustainable Development Goals, not on international trade.

s: For which time was India elected unopposed to the UN Human Rights Council for 2026–28?
x: India was elected for the 7th time, unopposed, for 1 January 2026 – 31 December 2028.

s: Where is International IDEA, which India chairs from 1 January 2026, headquartered?
x: International IDEA (est. 1995) is headquartered in Stockholm.

s: From which country did India take over the BRICS presidency for 2026?
x: India holds the BRICS presidency from 1 January to 31 December 2026, taking over from Brazil.

s:
Consider the following statements about the UN bodies in which India sits from 2026:
1. The UN Human Rights Council has 47 members and is based in Geneva.
2. ECOSOC has 54 members.
3. UNHRC members may serve any number of consecutive terms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: UNHRC has 47 members (Geneva) and ECOSOC 54; UNHRC members may serve at most two consecutive terms.

s: How many members does the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) have?
x: ECOSOC, one of the six principal UN organs, has 54 members elected for three years; India is a member for 2026-28.

s: In which year was the UN Human Rights Council established?
x: The UNHRC was set up in 2006 with 47 members and is based at Geneva; India began its 7th term in 2026.

s: Which country holds the chair of the Colombo Process for 2024-26?
x: India assumed the chair of the Colombo Process for 2024-26 in May 2024, for the first time.

s: With which subject does the Colombo Process deal?
o: Overseas employment and contractual labour of Asian countries of origin
Maritime security in the Indian Ocean
x: The Colombo Process is a regional consultative process of Asian countries of origin on overseas employment and contractual labour; its secretariat is hosted by IOM.

s: How many times has India been a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council?
x: India has served eight times as a non-permanent member.

s: Which countries were elected as new non-permanent members of the UN Security Council for 2026–27?
o: Bahrain, Colombia, DR Congo, Latvia and Somalia
Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama and Somalia
Algeria, Guyana, South Korea, Sierra Leone and Slovenia
Bahrain, Colombia, DR Congo, Latvia and Liberia
x: The new members for 2026–27 are Bahrain, Colombia, DR Congo, Latvia and Liberia. Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama and Somalia are continuing members.

s: Which country backed India's claim for permanent membership of the United Nations Security Council?
x: Chile backed India's permanent membership claim, with Ambassador Juan Angulo associated with the support. Germany, Japan and Brazil are members of the G4, but they are not the country identified in this support statement.

s: Which country is serving its first-ever term on the UN Security Council in 2026–27?
x: Latvia is the first-time member among the five elected for 2026–27.

s: Which of the following was NOT newly elected to the UN Security Council for 2026–27?
x: Pakistan is a continuing member elected in 2024; Bahrain, Colombia, DR Congo, Latvia and Liberia are new.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the G4?
x: The G4 are India, Germany, Japan and Brazil.

s: In which city was the Maritime Labour Convention 2006, the 'Seafarers' Bill of Rights', adopted at the International Labour Conference?
x: The MLC 2006 was adopted on 23 February 2006 at the International Labour Conference in Geneva, not London.

s: Which of the following about the Maritime Labour Convention 2006 is INCORRECT?
o: It is known as the "Seafarers' Bill of Rights".
It is regarded as the third pillar of international maritime law.
It is enforced through Flag State–Port State inspections.
It was adopted at the International Labour Conference in Geneva.
x: The MLC 2006 is regarded as the fourth pillar, not the third pillar, of international maritime law. It is enforced through Flag State–Port State inspections.

s: The Maritime Labour Convention 2006 is described as which pillar of international maritime law?
x: The MLC 2006 is called the 'fourth pillar' of international maritime law; it consolidated 60+ earlier ILO maritime conventions.

s: In which year was the International Labour Organization established?
x: The ILO, a tripartite body based at Geneva, was set up in 1919.

s: The India–Netherlands Hydrogen Fellowship Programme is a partnership between 19 IITs and which university?
x: The programme, launched on 6 February 2026 under DST, links the University of Groningen with 19 IITs on green hydrogen.

s: What amount did IGGEFIL sanction to Swarna Solar Ltd for a 100 MW solar project in Zambia?
x: IGGEFIL sanctioned USD 22.5 million to Swarna Solar Ltd. The 100 MW figure refers to the solar project’s capacity, not the loan amount.

s: In which year was the UN World Food Programme, with which India signed a five-year rice supply agreement, established?
x: The WFP was established in 1961; 1965 is the year the Food Corporation of India was set up.

s: At which event was the India–UK Offshore Wind Taskforce launched?
x: The Offshore Wind Taskforce was launched at the 4th India–UK Energy Dialogue and operates under the India–UK Vision 2035 framework.

s: For postings of up to how long does the India–UK Social Security Contributions Agreement avoid double social-security contributions?
x: The agreement, signed in New Delhi, avoids double social-security contributions for postings of up to 36 months.

s: The initial offshore-wind zones under the India–UK Offshore Wind Taskforce are Gujarat and which other state?
x: Gujarat and Tamil Nadu are the initial zones; ₹7,453 crore is the VGF for early projects.

s: Where is the UN World Food Programme, which signed a rice supply agreement with India, headquartered?
x: The WFP (est. 1961) is headquartered in Rome; its Executive Director is Cindy McCain.

s: Which UN body, headquartered at Rome, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020?
x: The World Food Programme (1961, Rome) won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020; India signed a five-year rice supply agreement with it.

s: Who is the Executive Director of the UN World Food Programme?
x: Cindy McCain is the Executive Director of the WFP.

s: Which exit of the US from UNESCO is the one announced in January 2026?
x: It is the US's third UNESCO exit, after 1984 and 2017.

s:
Consider the following statements about US withdrawals in January 2026:
1. A memorandum listed 66 bodies to quit, both UN and non-UN.
2. The US left the Paris Agreement for the first time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The memorandum covered 66 bodies (35 non-UN + 31 UN); the US left the Paris Agreement a second time.

s: How many members does the World Health Organization have?
x: The WHO (est. 7 April 1948, HQ Geneva) has 194 members.

s: The USA is the first country to attempt formal withdrawal from which treaty?
x: The US is the first country to attempt formal withdrawal from the UNFCCC.

s: Who signed the law legalising cryptocurrency mining and trading in Turkmenistan from January 2026?
x: Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdimuhamedow signed the law; it took effect from January 2026 with licences issued by the central bank.

s: Which of the following pairs related to the Gaza Peace Council is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Gaza National Governing Council was a 15-member body, not 25. The council was announced on Truth Social, Mladenov was Executive Committee Director-General and Ajay Banga a member.

s: Under Indonesia's revised Criminal Code in force from 2 January 2026, up to how long can extramarital sex be punished with imprisonment?
x: Extramarital sex carries up to one year; cohabitation carries up to six months.

s: Which of the following about Ecuador's 60-day state of emergency is INCORRECT?
o: It was signed by President Daniel Noboa on 31 December.
It was declared in Ecuador, whose capital is Guayaquil.
It covered nine provinces and three municipalities.
It included the provinces of Guayas, Manabí and Pichincha.
x: Ecuador's capital is Quito, not Guayaquil. The emergency, signed by Daniel Noboa, covered nine provinces and three municipalities.

s: Under the Maastricht criteria for joining the Eurozone, government debt must be below what share of GDP?
x: Eurozone entry needs a deficit below 3% and debt below 60% of GDP, plus ERM II.

s: Who is the Director-General of the Executive Committee of the Gaza Peace Council chaired by Donald Trump?
x: Nikolay Mladenov is Director-General of the Executive Committee; Witkoff, Kushner, Blair and Ajay Banga are members.

s: In which year was the European Central Bank formed?
x: The ECB was formed in 1998; Bulgaria, an EU member since 2007, adopted the euro as the 21st country.

s: The Windsor Framework (2023) between the UK and the EU relates to which region?
x: The Windsor Framework amended the Northern Ireland Protocol, easing checks on goods moving from Great Britain to Northern Ireland.

s: Which was the first country to recognise the rights of nature in its national constitution?
x: Ecuador's 2008 Constitution was the first national constitution to recognise the rights of nature (Pacha Mama), in Articles 71-74.

s: In which year did Ecuador adopt the constitution that first recognised the rights of nature?
x: Ecuador's constitution approved by referendum in September 2008 recognised the rights of nature.

s: What institutional milestone did the UNESCO Media and Information Literacy (MIL) Alliance reach in January 2026?
o: It elected its Global Board for the first time
It held its first Global MIL Week
x: The UNESCO MIL Alliance elected its Global Board for the first time in January 2026. The Cartagena Declaration came from Global MIL Week 2025, and its 300+ membership is a separate detail.

s: Where was the UNESCO Media and Information Literacy (MIL) Alliance launched in 2013?
x: The MIL Alliance was launched in 2013 at Abuja, Nigeria; it elected its first Global Board in January 2026.

s: Which World Heritage sites of Vietnam were mentioned when UNESCO sent emergency aid after Typhoons Wipha, Buoloay and Matmo?
o: Ha Long Bay and My Son
x: UNESCO gave about USD 740,000 in emergency aid to Vietnam; the World Heritage sites of Hue and Hoi An were affected.

s: Where was the 20th session of UNESCO's Intergovernmental Committee on Intangible Cultural Heritage, which inscribed Deepavali in December 2025, held?
x: The 20th ICH Committee session was held at the Red Fort, New Delhi (8-13 Dec 2025); Deepavali was inscribed on 10 December 2025.

s: Which Indian festival was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in December 2025?
x: Deepavali was inscribed on 10 December 2025 at the ICH Committee session in New Delhi.

s: In which category was Lucknow added to the UNESCO Creative Cities Network in 2025?
x: Lucknow became a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy on World Cities Day 2025, India's second after Hyderabad.

s: Which Indian city became India's first UNESCO 'City of Literature'?
x: Kozhikode was declared India's first UNESCO City of Literature; Gwalior joined as a City of Music in the same round.

s: Which of the following became the fifth country in WHO's Eastern Mediterranean Region to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem
Which country withdrew from the World Health Organization after the mandatory one-year notice period?
x: The United States withdrew from the World Health Organization after the mandatory one-year notice period. Canada, Australia and India are not identified as having withdrawn in this development.

s: In February 2026, the WHO validated Libya for eliminating which disease as a public health problem?
x: Libya eliminated trachoma, becoming the 28th country worldwide and 8th in the Eastern Mediterranean Region.

s: Which became the first EU country validated by the WHO for eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis?
x: Denmark was validated on 27 February 2026, the first EU country.

s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement is the second instrument adopted under which Article of the WHO Constitution?
x: It is the second instrument under Article 19, after the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.

s:
Consider the following statements about the WHO Pandemic Agreement:
1. It was adopted by the World Health Assembly on 20 May 2025.
2. It is open for signature though the PABS annex is pending.
3. It enters into force after 60 ratifications.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: It was adopted on 20 May 2025 and needs 60 ratifications; it opens for signature only after the PABS annex is adopted.

s: In which country is MONUSCO, extended by the UN Security Council until 20 December 2026, the UN mission?
x: MONUSCO is in the DR Congo; the UNSC extended it unanimously in December 2025.

s: Which of the following UN peacekeeping missions is correctly matched?
x: UNIFIL is in Lebanon; MONUSCO is in DR Congo, MINURSO in Western Sahara and MINUSCA in the Central African Republic.

s: What growth did the IMF's World Economic Outlook Update of January 2026 project for India for FY26?
x: The IMF raised India's FY26 projection to 7.3%; the World Bank's GEP put it at 7.2%.

s: What world growth for 2026 did the World Bank's Global Economic Prospects (January 2026) project?
x: The GEP projected world growth at 2.6% for 2026, down from 2.7% in 2025.

s: How many members does the IMF have?
x: The IMF has 191 members.

s: The IMF's 16th General Review of Quotas needs the consent of members holding what share of quotas?
x: It needs consent from members with 85% of quotas; by October 2025 only 72.78% had consented.

s: Which currency has the smallest weight in the IMF's SDR basket?
x: The pound has 7.44%, just below the yen at 7.59%; the dollar (43.38%) has the largest.

s: WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala began a second four-year term in September 2025. Which country is she from?
x: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is from Nigeria; her second term began on 1 September 2025.

s: Where was the 13th WTO Ministerial Conference (2024), which kept the e-commerce moratorium only until MC14, held?
x: MC13 was held at Abu Dhabi in 2024; it kept the moratorium (in place since 1998) until MC14 or 31 March 2026.

s: The Dunkel Draft, the basis of the WTO, was the Draft Final Act of which round?
x: The Dunkel Draft (20 December 1991), named after GATT DG Arthur Dunkel, was the Uruguay Round Draft Final Act.

s: Which WTO box covers minimally trade-distorting support with no limit?
x: The Green Box covers minimally distorting support with no limit, including public stockholding for food security.

s: For disaster recovery in which state is the World Bank's USD 245 million READY-HP programme (February 2026)?
x: READY-HP is Resilient Action for Development and Disaster Recovery Himachal Pradesh.

s: Under the PABS annex of the WHO Pandemic Agreement, what share of their production must manufacturers make available to WHO in real time?
x: Under PABS, manufacturers give WHO real-time access to 20% of production of vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics.

s: What was Libya's position when WHO validated it for eliminating trachoma in February 2026?
x: Libya was the 28th country worldwide and the 8th in WHO's Eastern Mediterranean Region to eliminate trachoma.

s: On replacing the lev with the euro, which EU country in number did Bulgaria become to adopt the euro?
x: Bulgaria became the 21st EU country to adopt the euro after replacing the lev.
